ONCOLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-05-25
57F, ambulatory visit for routine oncology follow-up.

S:
Patient returns to clinic for a scheduled check-up during ongoing treatment. She reports that the past two weeks have been tiring, with low energy for a few days after each infusion that gradually improves. Nausea has been mild and controlled with the antiemetics prescribed last cycle. Appetite is fair and she is keeping up with fluids. She works as an office administrator and has tried to stay on the job between cycles. She reports being unable to keep a regular work schedule and missed 6 days of work last month. No shortness of breath. Sleep is broken but improving. She lives with her spouse, who helps with transportation to appointments.

O:
BP 118/72, HR 80, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 148 lb, down 2 lb from prior.
General: alert, comfortable, no acute distress.
HEENT: oral mucosa moist, no ulceration.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Breast/chest wall: surgical site well healed, no erythema.
Extremities: no edema, port site clean and intact.
Labs (this week): Hgb 11.8 g/dL, ANC 1.9, platelets 180, comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits.

A/P:
1. Malignant neoplasm of breast, currently receiving chemotherapy. Tolerating current regimen with manageable side effects. Continue planned cycle schedule; next infusion as scheduled. Antiemetic regimen reviewed and refilled. Encouraged hydration and a symptom diary between visits.
2. Supportive care: counts reviewed and acceptable to proceed. Reinforced neutropenic precautions and when to call the clinic. Nutrition support discussed, with small frequent meals to maintain intake.
3. Function and work: discussed pacing activity around infusion days and realistic expectations for energy over each cycle. Provided documentation describing current activity limits for her employer.

Return to clinic for next scheduled infusion, sooner if new or worsening symptoms develop.
